lesson.text: Quick memory: can a muscle push, or can it only pull? (Only pull: muscles work in pairs.) Your muscles pull on your bones every time you run, jump, throw and catch.
Run tall: head up and eyes looking ahead. Bend your arms and swing them forwards and back, not across your body. Lift your knees and land on the front of your feet.
Jump: bend your knees and swing your arms back, then swing them forwards and up as you push off. Land softly on both feet with bent knees, like a spring squashing.
Throw overarm: stand side-on to the target and point at it with your other hand. Take the ball back high, step forward with the opposite foot, throw, and follow through towards the target.
Catch: watch the ball all the way into your hands. Make a basket with your fingers spread. Then 'give' with the ball, pulling it in to your chest so it does not bounce out.
Get better little by little. Start close to a partner, and after 5 catches in a row, take one step back. Everyone improves at their own speed: count your own best, not other people's.

Try it in the world: build a running track with a start line and a finish line. Add a long jump pit of sand with a marker every block. Then practise for real in a park or garden: how far can you jump?

exercises.prompt: When you run, where should your eyes look?
exercises.explain: Look ahead: it keeps your head up and your body tall, and you can see what is coming.

exercises.prompt: Swinging your arms helps you run faster.
exercises.hint: Try running with your arms stiff at your sides. Is it easier?
exercises.explain: True: bent arms swinging forwards and back help drive you along.

exercises.prompt: How should you land after a jump?
exercises.hint: Think of a spring squashing down.
choices: softly on both feet, knees bent
exercises.explain: Land softly on both feet and bend your knees, like a spring. It keeps your joints safe.

exercises.prompt: When a ball comes to you, it is best to close your eyes.
exercises.hint: How can you catch what you cannot see?
exercises.explain: False: watch the ball all the way into your hands.

exercises.prompt: Put the overarm throw in order.
exercises.hint: Get into position first; the throw comes last.
items: step forward with your opposite foot
point at the target with your other hand
exercises.explain: Stand side-on, point at the target, step forward with your opposite foot, then throw and follow through.

exercises.prompt: Zara throws with her right hand. Which foot should she step forward with?
exercises.hint: It is the foot on the opposite side.
exercises.explain: The opposite foot: her left. It turns her body and adds power to the throw.

exercises.prompt: Why do you pull the ball in to your chest as you catch it?
choices: so it does not bounce out
to hide it from your team
exercises.explain: Giving with the ball slows it down gently, so it stays in your hands instead of bouncing out.

exercises.prompt: Match each skill to its tip.
exercises.hint: Think of the picture on each lesson card.
exercises.explain: Run: swing bent arms. Jump: bend your knees and swing your arms up. Throw: point at the target. Catch: watch the ball in.

exercises.prompt: To jump further, swing your arms forwards and up as you push off.
exercises.hint: What do your arms do in the jump pictures?
exercises.explain: True: swinging your arms forwards and up carries your body with them.

exercises.prompt: Bram's catches keep bouncing out of his hands. What should he try?
choices: pulling the ball in as he catches
keeping his hands stiff and flat
looking away at the last moment
exercises.explain: Giving with the ball, pulling it in to his chest, slows it down so it stays in his hands.

exercises.prompt: Mimi's throws keep going off to one side. What should she check?
exercises.hint: Where should her other hand and her follow-through go?
choices: that she points at the target
that she stands on one foot
exercises.explain: Pointing at the target, stepping towards it and following through towards it sends the ball straight.

exercises.prompt: Is each tip for jumping or for catching?
items: make a basket with your hands
pull it in to your chest
exercises.hint: Which tips are about your hands and a ball?
exercises.explain: Jumping: bend your knees, swing your arms up, land softly. Catching: watch the ball, make a basket with your hands, pull it in.

exercises.prompt: Tilly can make 5 catches in a row from 2 steps away. What is a good next challenge?
exercises.hint: A good challenge is a little harder, not a lot harder.
exercises.explain: One step back is a little harder: she can still succeed, and she keeps improving.

exercises.prompt: Put the standing long jump in order.
exercises.hint: Where are your arms at the start?
items: swing your arms forward and push off
bend your knees and swing your arms back
exercises.explain: Bend and swing your arms back, swing them forward and push off, fly, then land softly on both feet.

exercises.prompt: Sort the tips: for running, or for throwing?
items: land on the front of your feet
exercises.hint: Which tips are about moving your legs, and which about aiming a ball?
exercises.explain: Running: head up, lift your knees, land on the front of your feet. Throwing: stand side-on, point at the target and follow through.
